findings: XDG ScreenCast v6 session lifecycle is a suitable Linux host-native authorization/session layer beneath F2 CaptureOwner, not an authority replacement.
Raw PipeWire node id is explicitly unsuitable as durable native stream identity because node ids can be reused; pipewire-serial/object.serial is the stronger native stream-instance discriminator.
Restore token is a restoration capability/request, not proof of current permission.

libportal is a viable thin wrapper candidate: it exposes session state/closed signal, restore lifecycle, raw a(ua{sv}) stream properties and PipeWire remote fd, allowing pipewire-serial extraction without adopting a heavyweight media framework.

Proposed F2 boundary remains stable PerceptionSource -> host-native session evidence -> HostPermissionGrant -> effective capability snapshot -> CaptureOwnerLease -> PipeWire buffer -> bounded CaptureFrameRef.
Native close/client loss/PipeWire error/serial replacement must invalidate the current host grant/owner before another frame is published; reopen/restoration requires an F2 source-generation advance.
Synthetic E3 state-machine replay passed 9/9 declared cases with canonical result digest af5f95a9269ea3ec8ea3448995d9c0e60e41dc75b001bb8be3fcee06adc89771.
counterhypothesis: A more mature wrapper path may still outperform libportal+direct PipeWire on implementation robustness. E3 did not compare real compositor/backend behavior or buffering/cleanup under actual capture.
next_exact_gate: E4 real F2 ablation/integration discriminator: compare libportal+PipeWire against one mature wrapper path on an admitted local target-relevant surface, measuring session close/revoke handling, pipewire-serial extraction and stale-target rejection, generation fencing, bounded buffer handoff, cleanup and latency/freshness.
